title: In-place array update
summary: Proves the compiler's in-place templates for set!, eraseIdxIfInBounds, and insertIdx! on an owned array at its last use: one store; a loop that moves the later elements down and a shorter length; and a move to a block of twice the capacity when full, a loop that moves the later elements up from the top down, the new element, and a longer length.
premises: heap.Owned for the array the call hands over, and Heap.At
A memory cap of at most 65,535 pages, and alloc and release at functions 0 and 1, for insertIdx!
Locals for the length, the loop, and the growth path below scratch and apart from the array, position, and value
result: Stmt.AppendPost for the updated array: owned at the same pointer, or for an insert into a full block at a new one, with every array apart from the old block kept and apart from the result.
